A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftMoE tokenization study. Their text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained material across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Atari experiments on tokenization, expert scaling, routing, pruning, and resets, including additional results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original Atari results and adds experiments including Procgen, SAC on CALE, pooling controls, and further component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 5 extends the tokenized Rainbow-lite variant from the PerConv reshape [h*w,d] to also support PerFeat [d,h*w], followed by sum or mean aggregation. The central SoftMoE routing, single-expert construction, and reset procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The original ALE and Atari100k coverage is retained. v2 Appendix C adds evaluation on 16 easy Procgen environments and CALE, extending coverage to another environment family and to visual tasks with continuous actions.

E2.justification: v2 adds PerFeat sum/average variants to the Rainbow-lite comparison in Figure 5, an unscaled SoftMoE-1 comparator to Figure 6, and global-average-pooling baselines in Figure 15. These expand comparisons within the existing architectural families.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce pooling-versus-flattening controls at default and 4x width, a quarter-width SoftMoE-1, and Procgen scoring normalized using Rmin/Rmax. Existing Atari budgets and Table 1 settings are retained. The newly disclosed reset-tuning procedure does not establish a revision to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence: global average pooling tests the flattening explanation, DER component ablations test whether Rainbow findings transfer, and a quarter-width expert tests the dependence on parameter count. It also adds PerFeat Rainbow-lite ablations and extends expert/router-reset comparisons to DQN. The original routing and pruning analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent seeds and 95% stratified bootstrap confidence intervals in Section 4.1. The additional results introduce no different stated run count, uncertainty estimator, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for PerFeat Rainbow-lite, pooling, reduced expert width, DER component ablations, DQN resets, Procgen, CALE, and per-game learning curves. These substantially enlarge the reported evidence. The new CALE results in Figure 22 favor tokenization by IQM but favor the baseline by mean, so they do not show uniform gains across metrics.

T1.justification: The RL definitions and mathematical background are substantively unchanged, and neither version supplies new theoretical propositions or proofs. The newly stated default slot-count formula documents an implementation setting rather than introducing a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same central claims about tokenization, single-expert performance, and expert redundancy. v2's conclusion adds a tentative extension of the findings to actor-critic agents in continuous-control environments, supported by the new CALE experiment.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the initial CALE results as supporting applicability to visual actor-critic control. Appendix B.5.2 also narrows the statement that resetting fails to improve utilization to Rainbow and DQN, while retaining DER's benefits. The spatial-structure explanation and DQN/categorical-loss caveats largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies default slots as #tokens/#experts and clarifies that reduced slot counts stay fixed during training. Appendix B.5.2 discloses the six tuning games, reset-period search grid, S&P candidates, and selected S&P values of (0.5, 0.5). These are additional disclosures; the hardware, software framework, and main hyperparameter table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cobbe et al. (2019) for Procgen and Farebrother and Castro (2024) for CALE. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier SoftMoE research remain substantially unchanged; other reference edits mainly concern formatting or bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Most main-text paragraphs and the section sequence are retained. Local edits clarify slots, repair the DQN/DER passage, expand cross-references, and refine explanations. Appendix B gains additional subsections, and Appendix C organizes the new environments and per-game results.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes the title/author presentation and document layout throughout. Figure 5 is reorganized by scaling and expanded for PerFeat; Figures 13–14 gain panels. Old Figures 15–17 persist as Figures 18–20, with the last expanded for DQN, alongside new control, environment, and per-game figures.

improvement.justification: The pooling and reduced-width controls, broader environment evaluations, tuning disclosures, and per-game curves strengthen v1's already extensive empirical investigation and improve transparency. The gains remain incremental: the central explanation is largely retained, Appendix C provides limited implementation detail, and CALE benefits depend on the metric. Overall, v2 offers better support and documentation without resolving a foundational deficiency.
